findings.title: Revalidate fingerprints before serving cache hits
findings.comment: The repository/workflow fingerprint is captured once at runWorkflow entry. A cache hit at engine.mjs:163-167 returns immediately without recomputing it, so an edit made after the resume guard—during an earlier leaf, semaphore wait, or before workflow import—can reuse a success produced from the old tree.

findings.title: Pass the pinned review base to every finder
findings.comment: Each finder receives the symbolic base ref, while resolvePin/pinDrift retain only merge-base and HEAD. journal.mjs explicitly treats both merge-base and base-tip as native-review identity; therefore a non-ancestor base-tip advance after a finder completes is missed by the panel gate and results for the prior target can be published.

findings.title: Include workflow runtime code in the fingerprint
findings.comment: workflowExtraPaths includes the workflow directory, sibling JS modules, and its lib subtree only. It excludes engine.mjs, codex.mjs, journal.mjs, and other runtime dependencies, so a later runtime version can accept the old fingerprint and replay results generated under materially different execution semantics.

findings.title: Stamp queued worker PIDs before requiring verification
findings.comment: spawnDetachedTaskWorker returns a PID, but queuedRecord persists no processStartTime. Both cancel and SessionEnd require pidInstanceVerified, so they cannot signal this queued child; task-worker subsequently reads the still-present request without checking cancelled status and can transition back to running.

findings.title: Publish workers.json atomically
findings.comment: workers.json is truncated and rewritten in place at engine.mjs:141-142. SIGKILL during that write makes JSON.parse fail; killWorkflowWorkers then returns [] and a later save overwrites the recovery evidence, leaving orphan workers unaddressable.

findings.title: Sweep workers when the workflow parent is already gone
findings.comment: The parent verification failure continues before the workflow-specific killWorkflowWorkers call. Cleanup nevertheless filters the session row afterward, so a dead/reused—or temporarily unverifiable—parent causes its independently stamped live workers to be skipped and their runDir pointer to disappear from the ledger.

findings.title: Quiesce workflow writers before deleting session rows
findings.comment: cleanupSessionJobs signals inside updateState's locked mutation. The workflow SIGTERM handler calls lifecycle.finalize, whose writeJobFile precedes its contended upsertJob; cleanup can delete the row/artifacts and then the delayed upsert re-inserts the cancelled row after the lock is released. No tombstone or generation check rejects it.

findings.title: Verify broker identity with the kill-path predicate
findings.comment: brokerInstanceIsOurs requires a stored stamp but delegates comparison to pidInstanceAlive, whose fail-open current-start-time read is appropriate for liveness, not signalling. A transient unreadable start time therefore authorizes terminateProcessTree against a possibly reused PID and its process group.

findings.title: Drain pending start responses before treating exit as failure
findings.comment: AppServerClientBase.handleExit immediately rejects and removes all pending RPCs. Node's child exit event may precede delivery/closure of buffered stdout, so a buffered turn/start or review/start response finds no pending entry when later parsed; captureTurn never reaches its post-start exit-drain race.

findings.title: Preserve completed native-review output on transport close
findings.comment: A completed exitedReviewMode item populates reviewText but never finalAnswerSeen. After stream drain, completionLostToExit salvages only finalAnswerSeen with drained collaborations/subagent turns, so valid native-review output is rejected if transport closes before turn/completed.

findings.title: Publish resume ownership before dead-job repair
findings.comment: Resume acquires the run lease at line 990 but does not publish its new PID to the ledger until lifecycle.register at line 1025. repairDeadWorkflowJobs ignores the lease, so a concurrent reader can finalize the old dead-PID row as failed and return it before the resumer later rewrites the same job as running.

findings.title: Commit per-job and ledger records as one generation
findings.comment: workflowJobLifecycle.persist writes the per-job record and ledger in separate operations. A resumed terminal run can therefore leave a durable running job file beside its prior terminal ledger if interrupted between them; repair skips terminal ledger rows, and result --json exposes the two incompatible generations directly.

findings.title: Revalidate the job before committing cancellation
findings.comment: resolveCancelableJob returns an unlocked running snapshot, after which interruptAppServerTurn and signalling can take time. There is no locked status/PID-generation recheck before cancellation writes, so natural completion can commit first and then be overwritten as cancelled, including mixed per-job/ledger interleavings.

findings.title: Settle cleanup when broker initialization creates no socket
findings.comment: parseBrokerEndpoint executes before this.socket is assigned. If it throws, connect's catch awaits close(); broker close has no no-socket settlement path and waits forever on exitPromise, which only socket error/close handlers resolve.

findings.title: Account for non-HEAD Git refs in repository identity
findings.comment: repoContent hashes HEAD, its diff, untracked blobs, and submodule state, but no other ref resolutions. An unchanged prompt that reads a literal mutable ref such as main therefore retains the same leaf key after that ref moves and can receive its prior answer.

findings.title: Avoid signalling the workflow PID twice
findings.comment: handleCancel ignores terminateProcessTree's delivered result and unconditionally sends a second direct SIGTERM for workflows. If the first process-group signal was delivered, the original verification is stale by the second call; unlike SessionEnd, this path permits a successor PID to be signalled after a rapid exit/reuse.

findings.title: Add an end-of-options boundary for the base ref
findings.comment: resolvePin passes args.base directly after git merge-base with no option boundary or validation. For example, git merge-base --octopus HEAD resolves successfully to HEAD in this checkout, so the baseCommit guard accepts an option as a ref and starts a panel against an unintended target.

findings.title: Hash untracked paths with a lossless delimiter
findings.comment: Both top-level and submodule untracked enumeration use newline-delimited, default-quoted Git output. A quoted non-ASCII/control-character filename is passed literally to hash-object, which fails and yields the constant unreadable marker; subsequent content changes then leave repoContent unchanged.

coverage.lens: Scrutinize resume correctness across journal cache keys, repository fingerprints, workflow fingerprints, and pinned review targets. Changed code or Git refs must not reuse stale worker results.
Trace process ownership across PID stamps, leases, state locks, cancellation, worker cleanup, and app-server shutdown. Look for races that leak workers or signal reused PIDs.
Check app-server event correlation and exit draining under concurrent workflow workers. Late notifications, stray stdout, or transport closure must not lose output or complete the wrong turn.
Audit durable job transitions across per-job records, the global ledger, the run journal, resume, and dead-job repair. Crashes and concurrent readers must not produce contradictory terminal state.
Review path containment and argument-injection boundaries in workflow loading, run identifiers, persisted job paths, and developer-instruction config overrides.
